From Ukrainian President Zelensky:
Volodymyr Zelenskyy / Володимир Зеленський (@ZelenskyyUa)
We had a very detailed discussion with @vonderleyen on virtually all the current areas of our work with the European Union and the decisions needed to support Ukraine. I thanked Ursula for the recent €1.24 billion tranche for defense, which Ukraine has already received. I am grateful for the confirmation that another approximately €3 billion in military support will be allocated as early as next week. These funds will strengthen us.
Of course, I briefed the President on the brutal Russian strikes that continue unabated. Just before our conversation, the Russians struck a power plant in Kyiv with a “shahed” drone, and many districts experienced power outages. Later, there were strikes on energy facilities in the Kharkiv region. And all of this happened AFTER the President of the United States made his statement about an energy ceasefire.
Under these circumstances, reliable support from our partners means real protection for people's lives and a guarantee that the Russians will not be able to break Ukraine. We deeply appreciate all the tangible steps taken to support our defense and our people.
Ursula and I agreed that our teams will have detailed discussions on our next joint actions and the coordination of our steps. We are also preparing to open the negotiating clusters – so that all the remaining clusters are opened by the end of the year. Ukraine’s European path is also a path toward strengthening Europe itself. Thank you!
— http://nitter.meowing.monster/ZelenskyyUa/status/2109335243417133188#m

Я подякував Урсулі за нещодавній транш у розмірі 1,24 млрд євро на оборону, який Україна вже отримала. Я вдячний за підтвердження того, що наступного тижня буде виділено ще близько 3 мільярдів євро військової підтримки. Ці кошти зміцнять нас.

Буквально напередодні нашої розмови росіяни вдарили з «шаха» по електростанції в Києві, у багатьох районах сталося знеструмлення. Ryan O'Leary (@RyanO_ChosenCoy)
One thing that is becoming more common is “PMC” type and drone companies hiring foreigners who did drones in Ukraine for work. The main problem with that, is that anyone can learn to fly a drone in 14-21 days. Give them 6 weeks and they’ll be hitting targets. What they don’t learn in-depth typically is the tactics behind drones (especially for the 6 monthers) or get a good grasp on signals/frequency and all the overly nerdy shit involved in that realm.
Not understanding frequencies and drone tactics in general will create a lot of scenarios such as this as outside of the Ukrainian war, front areas are not saturated with signals and hundreds of drones flying around so it’s much more easy to pinpoint launch positions and also signal locations.

У Латинській Америці, Африці та на Близькому Сході ми бачимо ранні війни безпілотників. Я б прирівняв це до того, де були Україна та Росія у 2023 році. Розповсюдження технологій і тактики безпілотників зростатиме, особливо коли закінчиться російсько-українська війна. Я сумніваюся, що ми готові.
Райан О'Лірі (@RyanO_ChosenCoy)
Одна річ, яка стає все більш поширеною, — компанії типу «PMC» і дрони, які наймають для роботи іноземців, які виготовляли дрони в Україні. Основна проблема полягає в тому, що кожен може навчитися керувати дроном за 14-21 день. Дайте їм 6 тижнів, і вони досягнуть цілей. Ryan O'Leary (@RyanO_ChosenCoy)

In May, Russia manoeuvred four military satellites, known as Cosmos 2610 through 2613, close to a commercial radar-imaging satellite, according to the US Space Force. Finland's ICEYE, which supplies data to the US and its allies, confirmed to Reuters that it was one of their satellites. Major General Michael Traut, ​head of German space command, described the Russian spacecraft as “chasing” the ICEYE satellite, which provides battlefield intelligence imagery. 'Russia is demonstrating ways, ​which, if employed directly towards a mega constellation like Starlink, could have an impact on their lifetime' and on ⁠the quality of service for all users, not just Ukraine, General Traut told Reuters. He said satellite capabilities could be disrupted even without a ​direct attack. That 'concerns me quite a lot,' he said." https://www.reuters.com/business/media-telecom/russian-satellite-activity-raises-concerns-starlink-german-space-commander-says-2026-10-09/
